nodes.description: Allogeneic HSCT is the only established cure for CGD: it replaces the hematopoietic compartment with donor cells that assemble a functional NADPH oxidase, correcting both the killing defect and the inflammatory arm. A 712-patient international study reports 3-year overall survival of 85.7%, and a prospective reduced-intensity-conditioning study - designed for adolescents, adults and high-risk patients, in whom graft failure and transplant-related mortality had been the obstacle - reports 93% overall survival at a median 21 months. Outcomes are worse with increasing age and with a mismatched donor, which is the basis for transplanting early and from a well-matched donor.

nodes.description: Infliximab closes fistulae and achieves complete or partial remission in most treated patients with steroid-dependent or refractory CGD inflammatory bowel disease, but it does so at a real infectious cost in a host that already cannot kill catalase-positive organisms: severe infections with typical CGD pathogens, and two deaths in the five-patient NIH series. It is best understood as a short-term bridge in selected patients, usually to transplantation, under aggressive antimicrobial prophylaxis and surveillance.

nodes.description: Lifelong daily antibacterial prophylaxis, standardly with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, is recommended to prevent infections. The retrospective NIH experience quantifies the benefit as roughly a three-to-fourfold fall in non-fungal infection rates in both autosomal and X-linked disease, with no increase in fungal infection - the concern that prompted that review. Pregnancy caution: trimethoprim (a folic acid antagonist) is discontinued during pregnancy because of the high risk for birth defects.

nodes.description: Gene editing corrects the patient's own mutation in situ rather than adding a transgene, which avoids both a donor and a randomly integrating vector. PM359 corrects the recurrent NCF1 exon 2 GT deletion that causes most p47phox-deficient CGD by prime editing of autologous CD34+ cells: two treated participants engrafted promptly and showed NADPH oxidase activity in neutrophils within a month, sustained to last follow-up at six and four months. A separate adenine base-editing approach corrects the prototypical CYBB c.676C>T mutation in patient HSPCs at up to 70% efficiency and has entered a first-in-human trial. Both are early-phase: two participants and a few months of follow-up are a demonstration of engraftment and oxidase activity, not of clinical benefit or long-term safety.

nodes.description: CGD macrophages and monocytes recruit almost no LC3 to the phagosome, so LC3-associated phagosome handling is defective. This matters therapeutically because the autophagy defect is what links the oxidase lesion to excess IL-1 beta release, and because both IL-1 receptor blockade and mTOR inhibition act at this point rather than on the oxidase.

nodes.description: The assembled NADPH oxidase normally catalyzes the respiratory (oxidative) burst, reducing molecular oxygen to superoxide, which is dismutated and converted to hydrogen peroxide, hypohalous acids, and other reactive oxygen species within the phagosome. In CGD this burst is absent or markedly reduced, so phagocytes ingest microbes but fail to generate the oxidants required for efficient microbicidal activity.

nodes.description: Transfused donor granulocytes supply phagocytes that can mount an oxidative burst, as an adjunct to antimicrobials and surgery in severe or refractory infection. The NIH experience favours early, frequent and sustained courses. The cost is alloimmunization: in patients who later proceeded to transplantation or gene therapy, pre-procedure transfusions were associated with anti-HLA antibodies, primary graft failure and early immune-mediated cytopenia, so their use has to be weighed against a planned cellular therapy. Transfusions given after transplantation did not carry that association.

nodes.description: A distinct and counterintuitive use of steroids in CGD: hepatic abscesses were traditionally managed by open surgery or percutaneous drainage, and corticosteroids given with antibiotics resolve abscesses refractory to those measures. In the NIH series, time to a repeat hepatic intervention was longest in the corticosteroid-managed group. The rationale is that the lesion is substantially an inflammatory mass rather than drainable pus - which is why this is recorded against the inflammatory arm of the disease and not against the killing defect.

nodes.description: Immunomodulatory prophylaxis with recombinant interferon gamma-1b, given subcutaneously three times weekly, is part of the standard prophylactic regimen in many centers. The pivotal 128-patient randomized trial more than halved serious infections, and benefit was seen regardless of age, mode of inheritance, or concurrent antibiotic prophylaxis. Age is not recorded as an effect modifier below, because that trial names no age strata to compare: its participants had a median age of 15 years and the report states only that benefit held regardless of age. Crucially, the same trial found no measurable improvement in phagocyte superoxide production, so the mechanism of benefit is not oxidase restoration and remains unsettled (see the ifn_gamma_mechanism_in_cgd discussion). A later meta-analysis supports a reduced risk of serious infection while judging the overall evidence base insufficient.

nodes.description: Anakinra targets the IL-1 axis that is left running in CGD because the autophagy defect permits excess IL-1 beta release. nodes.description: A second, non-phagosomal consequence of the same lesion. In normal phagocytes NADPH oxidase activity signals through PPAR-gamma to drive mitochondrial reactive oxygen species production; in CGD phagocytes that mitochondrial oxidant pool is itself deficient. This node is the target of PPAR-gamma agonism (pioglitazone), which raises mitochondrial oxidants without repairing the NADPH oxidase, and is therefore a separate point of intervention from the oxidase complex itself.

nodes.description: The most mechanistically interesting failed-so-far approach in CGD, and the reason two nodes in this entry exist. Pioglitazone bypasses the NADPH oxidase entirely: by activating PPAR-gamma it raises mitochondrial oxidant production and restores efferocytosis in oxidase-deficient phagocytes. In gp91phox-null mice that was enough to improve killing of Staphylococcus aureus, and in human CGD monocytes it restored efferocytosis both ex vivo and in two patients treated for inflammatory bowel disease. The one prospective clinical attempt, in three patients with severe infection, was stopped for futility: no improvement in infection severity and no rise in the DHR stimulation index.

nodes.description: Posaconazole is used as an alternative to itraconazole for antifungal prophylaxis. Pediatric experience is limited and no dose is established from a trial; a weight-based twice-daily algorithm derived in children with CGD achieves adequate exposure. Recorded here as an alternative agent, not as a demonstrated reduction in fungal infection - no placebo-controlled prophylaxis trial of posaconazole in CGD is cited in this entry.

nodes.description: Mononuclear phagocytes lacking a functional oxidase still activate caspase-1 and release biologically active IL-1 beta, and do so more strongly than normal cells - so inflammasome activation in CGD proceeds without ROS rather than requiring it. This is the node that explains why a disease of absent oxidants is hyperinflammatory, and it is the target of IL-1 receptor blockade.

readouts.interpretation: The assay measures the output of the respiratory burst, so a low or absent value is the direct functional expression of this node. It does not identify which subunit is defective; that needs molecular testing.

readouts.interpretation: More residual production means less severe illness and better survival; the relationship holds as a continuous variable and independently of the affected gene, so it is not a restatement of genotype. Mortality curves separate after adolescence rather than in childhood.

nodes.description: The one randomized controlled trial of an anti-inflammatory agent for CGD-IBD. In a multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase II trial of eight male patients, thalidomide met its prespecified efficacy criterion with CGD-related infection rates comparable before and after treatment - the key question for any immunomodulator in this disease. The trial is very small, so the result establishes a signal and a safety impression rather than effectiveness.

nodes.description: Rapamycin was tried in CGD as an autophagy inducer, on the reasoning that the disease's inflammatory arm is driven by defective autophagy and consequent inflammasome activation. In cells from 15 patients it reversed the CGD inflammatory profile across monocyte, T-cell and neutrophil compartments, and its effect on IL-1 beta secretion was enhanced by adding anakinra. This is an ex vivo result that opens a therapeutic approach; no clinical trial in CGD is cited here, and the autophagy-induction step itself was the rationale rather than the measured endpoint, so no edge is drawn to the autophagy node.
